title: Labeled chip-firing on trees: the ballot conjecture is false
statement: In labeled chip-firing on the undirected k-ary tree with a root self-loop, starting from (k^l - 1)/(k - 1) labeled chips at the root, the ballot property (for every vertex and children a < b, the i-th smallest chip in the subtree of a is smaller than the i-th smallest in the subtree of b) fails for some stable configuration when (k, l) = (2,5) [31 chips, including at the root], (2,6), (2,7), (2,8), (3,4), (3,5), (4,4); explicit legal firing sequences are certified. This refutes Conjecture 3.7 (3.16 per the publisher) of Inagaki, Khovanova and Luo, on which the proof of their ballot bound rests, and Conjecture 5.1 of Inagaki and Lin (2025). The property holds for (2, l <= 4), (3, l <= 3), (4, l <= 3), proved by exhaustive search of a two-colour threshold projection.
resolves: Inagaki-Khovanova-Luo Conjecture 3.16 and Inagaki-Lin Conjecture 5.1 (both refuted by explicit certificates)
verified: check_ballot.py replays eight certificates (31, 31, 63, 127, 255 chips on the binary tree; 40, 121 on the ternary; 85 on the 4-ary): every firing legal, stable end with the expected shape, ballot violation; exhaustive two-colour search proves the property for (2, l <= 4), (3, l <= 3), (4, l <= 3); a corrupted certificate fails the replay.

Independent review (fresh agent): model and conjecture scope confirmed from both papers; all certificates replayed with independent code; exhaustive labeled search at 15 chips reproduces 36,220 stable configurations, none violating; independent two-colour search confirms the positive cases.

colour_census_relations.cpp at 31 chips, all thresholds: violating stable colour states exactly for t = 8..23 (1340 total); complete set of forced order relations chip(u) < chip(w): 196 (48 cover relations); at 15 chips 65 (20 cover relations). Hash-based visited sets; counts for t <= 12 match the unhashed search.

Independent literature audit (October 2026): both conjectures open, numbering confirmed (IKL Conjecture 3.16 in Ann. Comb. 30 (2026) = 3.7 in arXiv 2410.00039v1; Inagaki-Lin Conjecture 5.1 unchanged in v1 and v2), and the published verification covers only l = 3, 4, so the certificates here are the first cases tested.
unresolved: failure for every larger l (certified for binary l = 5..8, ternary l = 4, 5, 4-ary l = 4)
whether the ballot bound's inequality remains true
the number of stable configurations for l >= 5
nonclaims: no claim beyond the certified sizes
smallest_decisive_test: Replay a certificate under the stated rules; an illegal firing or absence of a violation would void it.
